questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane and never move from it.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other vehicles can see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as needed based on the road and traffic around you.

questions.question: If the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left portion of a lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
All areas of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of the lane. When wet, this area loses traction. You can ride beside this strip and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When deciding on a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center portion of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the right portion of the lane.
Be flexible and consider many different factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible and consider many different factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you can be seen best and keep space around you.

questions.question: If taking a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue, dress to stay warm and dry. Limit riding to no more than 6 hours per day and take rest breaks every 2 hours. Avoid caffeine because extreme fatigue follows when it wears off.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle's wind blast hits you, you will have the most room to recover if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space to recover if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: Studies show that most crash-involved riders:

options.text: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and do not brake the rear tire enough.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
Behind the rear axle.
On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or use saddlebags. High loads raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and change balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointed upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is generally:

options.text: Pairs.
A staggered formation.
A single-file line.
A pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, going around curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: You should maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. When conditions are poor, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction opposite of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction once you clear the hazard.

questions.question: Which instruction should NOT be given to a passenger before riding?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, your passenger should get on after the engine starts. They should sit as close forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the handholds, your waist, hips, or belt. Keep legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: Which option is NOT a way to prevent someone from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Get them involved in activities to slow their drinking and keep them busy while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends involved in stopping your friend from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To stop someone from driving intoxicated, arrange alternative transportation, involve them in other activities to slow drinking, keep them from leaving, and ask friends to help. Waiting 15 minutes after the last drink is not effective.

questions.question: When do you NOT need a larger space cushion while driving?

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
Traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance during poor conditions such as slippery pavement, reduced visibility, or heavy traffic. You can use normal distance when weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening your path.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane is usually safe when:

options.text: Never safe for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. This area is generally safe unless the road is wet. Since the strip is usually about two feet wide, you can often ride to one side and stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a good surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and down shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and travels in a straight line.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the best formation for a group of riders going through a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. While staggered formation is good for maintaining space in a group, single-file is safer for curves.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Not use it.
Use high beam.
Use low beam.
Switch between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use high beam.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. This helps other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Use high beam.
Use low beam.
Do not use your headlight.
Switch between high and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beam in rain, snow, or fog. High beam reflects off these conditions and makes it harder to see.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use high beam.
Use headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use high beam, follow other vehicles' headlights, and wear reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and stay safe. Do not stay only in the left part of your lane.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to see better and be more visible.
Stay in the center of the lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to see better and be more visible.
questions.explanation: Move to the left part of your lane when passing. This improves your view and makes you more visible to other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
